results.summary_before: This is a two-player countdown timer game where players must guess when a hidden timer reaches a target time. The game uses four buttons for start, reset, and player inputs, and displays the timer on a 7-segment display. After both players have pressed their buttons, the displayed times are shown. It requires an external PMOD 7-segment display and a PMOD button module for operation.

results.summary_before: This design is a simple leaky integrate-and-fire neuron implemented in Verilog that integrates an 8-bit input current into a membrane potential, leaks it over time, and fires a spike when a threshold is reached before resetting. The input current is applied on ui_in, the membrane state is exposed on uo_out, and the spike appears on uio[7]. The testing section only says 'Do something', so no concrete test procedure is documented. No external hardware is required, but the documentation is too thin to describe the implementation details beyond the general LIF behavior.

results.summary_before: This project implements a 6-bit input ALU that selects an operation based on a 4-bit RISC-V opcode and produces an 8-bit output. Inputs A and B are provided through the bidirectional pins and the dedicated input pins, while the opcode is set on the remaining input pins. Testing involves applying input values and opcodes and observing the output, optionally with LEDs connected for visual feedback. The design is a straightforward iterative ALU with no external hardware required.
